- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–8% in subsequent days, especially if sentiment drops.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often overreacts; dampen forecast slope and shift mean toward recent low.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is falling, model often underestimates drop; increase forecast downward by 1–4% to match true trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to lag in direction; align forecast with sentiment’s most recent 3-day trend, not 18-day average.
